commonNames.name: Assamese Macaque
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Assam macaque (Macaca assamensis) or Assamese macaque is a macaque of the Old World monkey family native to South and Southeast Asia. Since 2008, it has been listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List, as it is experiencing significant declines due to poaching, habitat degradation, and fragmentation.
wikipedia.title: Assam macaque

wikipedia.extract: Palaeopropithecus is a recently extinct genus of large sloth lemurs from Madagascar related to living lemur species found there today. Three species are known, Palaeopropithecus ingens, P. maximus, and P. kelyus.
wikipedia.title: Palaeopropithecus

commonNames.name: Pale Fork-marked Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The pale fork-marked lemur (Phaner pallescens), or western fork-marked lemur, is a species of lemur known from western Madagascar; south of the Fiherenana River to the region of Soalala. It is said to be the smallest fork-marked species.
wikipedia.title: Pale fork-marked lemur

wikipedia.extract: Grebes () are aquatic diving birds in the order Podicipediformes (). Grebes are widely distributed freshwater birds, with some species also found in marine habitats during migration and winter.
wikipedia.title: Grebe

wikipedia.extract: Nine families of largely arboreal birds make up the order Piciformes (), the best-known of them being the Picidae, which includes the woodpeckers and close relatives. The Piciformes contain about 71 living genera with a little over 450 species, of which the Picidae make up about half.
wikipedia.title: Piciformes

commonNames.name: Guinea Baboon
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Guinea baboon (Papio papio) is a baboon from the Old World monkey family. Some (older) classifications list only two species in the genus Papio, this one and the hamadryas baboon.
wikipedia.title: Guinea baboon

wikipedia.extract: The African bush elephant (Loxodonta africana), also known as the African savanna elephant, is a species of elephant native to sub-Saharan Africa and the largest living terrestrial animal, with fully grown bulls reaching an average shoulder height of 3.04–3.36 m (10.0–11.0 ft) and a body mass of 5.2–6.9 t (5.7–7.6 short tons); the largest recorded specimen had a shoulder height of 3.96 m (13.0 ft) and an estimated body mass of 10.4 t (11.5 short tons). It is characterised by its long prehensile trunk with two finger-like processes; a concave back; large ears which help reduce body heat; and sturdy tusks that are noticeably curved.
wikipedia.title: African bush elephant

wikipedia.extract: Myiopsitta is a genus of parrots in the family Psittacidae. They are native to southeastern South America, from Bolivia and southern Brazil, south to central Argentina.
wikipedia.title: Myiopsitta

wikipedia.extract: Oreopholus is a genus of bird belonging to the family Charadriidae. The tawny-throated dotterel (Oreopholus ruficollis) is the only extant species, although another species, Oreopholus orcesi, is known from the Late Pleistocene of Ecuador.
wikipedia.title: Oreopholus

wikipedia.extract: The Mexican spider monkey (Ateles geoffroyi vellerosus), also known by its mayan name "Ma'ax", is a subspecies of Geoffroy's spider monkey, and is one of the largest types of New World monkey. It inhabits forests of Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and Honduras.
wikipedia.title: Mexican spider monkey

commonNames.name: Black Bearded Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The black bearded saki (Chiropotes satanas) is a species of New World monkey, native to the Amazon rainforest of South America, specifically to an area of north-eastern Brazil. It is one of five species of bearded saki.
wikipedia.title: Black bearded saki

commonNames.name: Jalali Kabutor
commonNames.source: ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (EIA) OF WORLD BANK FINANCED SIDDHIRGANJ 450 MW COMBINED CYCLE POWER PLANT (CCPP) PROJECT SIDDHIRGANJ, NARAYANGAJ

wikipedia.extract: The rock dove (Columba livia), also known as the common pigeon or rock pigeon (but see also Petrophassa), is a member of the bird family Columbidae (doves and pigeons). In common usage, it is often simply referred to as the "pigeon", although the rock dove is the wild form of the bird; the pigeons familiar to most people are the domesticated forms of the wild rock dove.
wikipedia.title: Rock dove

commonNames.name: Black Mantle Tamarin; Graells's Black-mantled / Graells’s Tamarin (graellsi)

wikipedia.extract: The black-mantled tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis, is a species of saddle-back tamarin from the northwestern Amazon in far western Brazil, southeastern Colombia, north-eastern Peru and eastern Ecuador. There are 3 subspecies: Spix's black mantle tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis nigricollis Graells's tamarin or Graells' black-mantle tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis graellsi Hernandez-Camacho's black-mantle tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis hernandezi Graells's tamarin was previously considered to be a separate species.
wikipedia.title: Black-mantled tamarin

wikipedia.extract: Proconsul africanus was an ape which lived from about 23 to 14 million years ago during the Miocene epoch. It was a fruit eater and its brain was larger than that of a monkey, although probably not as large as that of a modern ape.
wikipedia.title: Proconsul africanus

wikipedia.extract: Heliadornis is a genus of prehistoric seabirds related to modern tropicbirds, but native to temperate climates. They lived in the Miocene.
wikipedia.title: Heliadornis

wikipedia.extract: Austral storm petrels, or southern storm petrels, are seabirds in the family Oceanitidae, part of the order Procellariiformes. These smallest of seabirds feed on planktonic crustaceans and small fish picked from the surface, typically while hovering.
wikipedia.title: Austral storm petrel

commonNames.name: Humboldt’s Squirrel Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Humboldt's squirrel monkey (Saimiri cassiquiarensis) is a species of squirrel monkey from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. It had previously been considered a subspecies of the common squirrel monkey, S. sciureus, but was elevated to full species status based on a genetic study by Carretero-Pinzón in 2009.
wikipedia.title: Humboldt's squirrel monkey
